variants.name: ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline + endpoint routing
variants.implementation_notes: ASP.NET Core composes the front controller from request delegates: app.Use registers stages that run before and after next.Invoke, app.Run installs the terminal handler, and endpoint routing (MapGet, MapControllers) is the dispatcher that selects the request-specific handler. What replaces the classic structure: one ordered pipeline of delegates replaces the FrontController class and its pre/post hooks, and the DI container supplies request-scoped services to the terminal handler. Keep in mind that mutating status or headers after the response has started throws.
pitfalls: Middleware order defines semantics: exception handling must be first, routing before endpoints, and an authorisation stage placed after MapGet silently never runs for matched requests.

Anything captured in a middleware constructor is created once for the application lifetime, so injecting scoped services there is a captive-dependency bug; take them as InvokeAsync parameters instead.
Writing to the body and then calling next.Invoke (or touching headers after start) corrupts the response or throws; check HasStarted and return instead.

variants.name: Classic ASP.NET HTTP module + handler factory (legacy)
variants.implementation_notes: In ASP.NET Framework the front controller is assembled from parts: an IHttpModule registered in Web.config is invoked for every request and subscribes to pipeline events (AuthenticateRequest, BeginRequest, EndRequest) for shared behaviour, while a wildcard IHttpHandler or an IHttpHandlerFactory maps the request to the endpoint that produces the response. What replaces the classic structure: the module replaces the controller pre/post hooks and the handler factory replaces the dispatcher - there is no single controller object. Use it only in legacy Framework code; the ASP.NET Core pipeline is the modern form of the same pattern.
pitfalls: Modules run for every request, including static files, so routing logic placed in a module couples unrelated endpoints.
Setting a status code in a module does not end the pipeline - the handler still runs unless the module calls CompleteRequest or redirects.
The handler factory controls reusability: IHttpHandler instances with IsReusable=true are pooled and must be stateless, otherwise request state leaks between users.
